newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Nine killed in Angolan military depot blast.
newsitem.headline: Nine killed in Angolan military depot blast.

text.p: Nine people were killed on Sunday when a military ammunition depot exploded outside the Angolan capital of Luanda, hospital officials said on Monday.
Sergio Romero, director of Luanda's Prenda Hospital, told Reuters four people died and seven others were wounded as a direct result of the midday explosion in the Viana suburb.
Five more people were killed and 15 others injured as people tried to escape from the area of the blast, believed to have been triggered by a fire.
"I can tell you that four were killed and seven injured by the explosion," Romero said.
"As for the other 20, I can't say, but they were brought into the clinic from the same area," he added.
Nurses said the survivors had reported they were hurt while running from the explosion, and that the five others had died in the panic.
Earlier a United Nations official had said five people were killed in the blast.
Residents said the explosion caused widespread panic.
"People were running everywhere. We all thought the enemy was attacking," she added.
Angola's 19-year civil war ended in 1994 when the MPLA-led government and former rebel UNITA movement signed a peace accord in the Zambian capital Lusaka to halt fighting.
At least half a million people are believed to have died in the war which erupted soon after independence from Portugal in 1975.
